it, and drive its core toward finer scales.  The global danger is whether that
flow can sharpen one of its own structures so far that smooth continuation
fails in finite time.  Fix one velocity \(u\), one pressure \(p\), and one
viscosity \(\nu>0\), and follow only that history:
first_divergence.mechanism: The first selection changes the requested reader movement. Thomas's supplied movement begins with the critical-height predicament, then uses a vortex to make that predicament concrete. This opening instead restarts from the governing PDE and follows it with a vorticity lesson and a scaling derivation before reaching critical height. For a reader arriving from the abstract and proof guide, that choice spends the opening on foundational setup and makes the vortex carry a question that has not yet been stated. The opening becomes an introductory mini-lecture instead of the candid, quick demonstration requested. Later inclusion of the requested topics does not repair this initial detour.
first_divergence.repair_constraint: Repair only the opening movement through the first critical-height and energy comparison. Begin with the requested below/above/at critical-height predicament, then let one vortex example carry that predicament into the finite-energy Zeno possibility. Keep the needed distinctions about scaling and viscosity inside that explanation; do not precede it with a separate PDE and vorticity primer.
